entries.title: Kramers' escape rate, overdamped (Smoluchowski) limit
entries.statement: For strong friction and a barrier high compared with kT, the rate of escape from a potential well is the geometric mean of the curvatures at the well bottom and the barrier top, divided by 2 pi times the friction coefficient, times the Arrhenius factor. It is too high by corrections of relative order kT/barrier: 3 to 6% at 10 kT for the cubic, quartic double-well and cosine shapes mapped here.

entries.title: Exact mean first-passage time in one dimension (quadrature formula)
entries.statement: The mean time for an overdamped particle in a potential U to leave an interval is a double integral of exp(U/kT) and exp(-U/kT): the Pontryagin-Andronov-Vitt formula. It holds at any barrier height and for any potential shape, and it is the exact reference against which rate formulas such as Kramers' are judged.
entries.formula: t(x) = \frac{1}{D}\int_x^b dy\, e^{U(y)}\int_a^y dz\, e^{-U(z)}\quad (a \text{ reflecting},\ b \text{ absorbing})

entries.notes: Question for the authors (Haenggi, Talkner and Borkovec). In Eq. (7.7) as printed (journal scan, p. 291), the inner integral in the numerator of the first term has exp[U(z)/kBT]. With that sign the formula does not vanish at the absorbing end: for U = x^3/3 - x on [-2, 1] with kT = D = 1 it gives t(b) = 2.511 instead of 0. With exp[-U(z)/kBT] it vanishes there and agrees with this entry to 1e-10. A flat potential cannot reveal the difference. We read this as a misprint but may have misread the notation: on the author-hosted scan we read, a speck sits on the sign, so the printed sign must be confirmed on a clean copy before the authors are asked. No erratum or comment was found in Crossref, PubMed or an OpenAlex search of citing works (15 Oct 2026).

entries.title: Distribution of the switching point under a ramp (quasi-static approximation)
entries.statement: When a control (a force, a current, a field) is ramped and the system escapes with the rate k(F) of the frozen value F, the switching value has density k(F)/Fdot exp(-integral of k/Fdot). This turns any rate law into switching-current, rupture-force or switching-field histograms, and is exact for a rate process; the rate picture itself fails for ramps that are fast compared with relaxation in the well.

entries.title: Force-dependent escape rate of Dudko, Hummer and Szabo
entries.statement: Under a constant force F, the escape rate over a barrier of height dG at distance x is k0 (1 - nu F x/dG)^(1/nu - 1) exp{dG [1 - (1 - nu F x/dG)^(1/nu)]/kT}: nu = 2/3 for a linear-cubic surface, 1/2 for a harmonic well with a cusp, and nu = 1 gives Bell's exponential law. For nu = 2/3 it is exactly Kramers' formula for the tilted surface, the large-barrier limit of the noisy saddle-node.

entries.title: Force-dependent lifetimes from rupture-force histograms (Dudko, Hummer and Szabo, 2008)
entries.statement: A histogram of rupture forces at one loading rate gives the lifetime of the bond at each force: the probability of surviving to that force divided by the density of ruptures there and the loading rate.
